prize_parts.citation: For the rational design of molecular-sieve catalysts, linking organic structure-directing agents, framework topology and active-site placement to catalytic function

statement.case_for: I keep B051 (Corma, Davis, Zones) as my preferred single-part configuration. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, which rests on a deliberate design chain: organic structure-directing agents choose the framework, framework topology and heteroatom or cation placement set the active site, and the active site sets the catalytic function. That chain is the basis of Cu-SSZ-13 NOx abatement, methanol-to-olefins, hydrocracking and many fine-chemical processes, and it has been confirmed independently for decades, so there is no maturity question of the kind every colleague raised against B063 and B068. The chair asked whether breadth of ranking should outweigh the merit of single-member candidates; I do not think breadth settles the matter, and I rest my case on the clarity of the principle and the verified impact. I did reweigh B063 seriously, because the three supporters agree on the same three names and the chemical mechanism is explicit. I still judge a prize for a validated design principle to be better supported this year than one for a modality whose first approval has not happened.
statement.case_against: Nobody else prefers B051 and its opening support is modest, so I may be over-weighting a field I work in. Attribution among Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis is subjective, and industrial zeolite work is patent-heavy. Colleagues (Aqvist, Somfai) are right that the 2025 framework-materials prize may make the committee reluctant to honour porous materials again so soon, although zeolites are an older, inorganic class with a different catalytic role. B063 is the only plurality position, with three supporters on identical names, and if a degrader is approved soon the timing objection falls away and I would have little ground to rank B051 above it. A two-part prize would be a way to avoid choosing between maturity and novelty, but I do not think B051 and B063 pair naturally.

responses.point: Prefers B063 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) as a new chemical modality that is mechanistically explicit and independently confirmed, while conceding that no degrader is approved and that Ciulli, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim have real claims.
responses.response: I accept that the mechanism is chemically explicit and well reproduced, and I answer the chair's question directly: I do not regard the absence of an approval as disqualifying in principle, but I would want at least one approved degrader or a pivotal-trial result before ranking the modality above a field whose payoff is already measured in industrial scale. My larger concern is the name set. Crews, Deshaies and Handa unite the PROTAC and cereblon strands, yet Ciulli's VHL ligands made PROTACs drug-like and Ito co-discovered cereblon's role, so the cut is more contestable than the unanimity among the three supporters suggests. I would keep B063 as my first alternative and would not oppose it if the committee moves there.

responses.point: Argues that PROTAC design and the cereblon-mediated molecular-glue mechanism are two halves of one story, and would place Handa ahead of Ciulli in a three-person cut.
responses.response: I find the Handa-over-Ciulli reasoning coherent for the mechanism of molecular glues, but it makes the citation depend on the glue strand, which is the part with the longest history and the clearest chemical explanation, while the PROTAC strand has the stronger design logic. Because the citation spans both strands, I think it is more exposed to the 'two discoveries' objection than your statement allows, and the omission of Ciulli then leaves the structure-guided design of drug-like degraders without a credited name. That does not make the case weak, but it is why I cannot yet treat the attribution as settled.

responses.point: Proposes a two-part prize pairing B035 (Cullis, Anderson) with B068 (Liu), and notes that the 2025 MOF prize may make the committee feel porous materials were just addressed.
responses.response: On the 2025 point I disagree in degree, not in substance. The MOF prize honoured reticular, designed framework chemistry; zeolite and molecular-sieve design is a different, older, inorganic class whose decisive claim is catalytic, not structural, so the new prize would not repeat the earlier citation. I do agree that the field's credit is diffuse and that the committee may still prefer to wait. On your configuration, I find the lipid carrier argument persuasive but I share your own reservation that both parts sit near medicine, and a Cullis plus Anderson pairing omits Hope and Madden, who did the Vancouver ionizable-lipid work.

responses.point: Prefers B035 with Cullis, Hope and Madden, as the carrier counterpart to the mRNA cargo recognised in 2023, grounded in lipid self-assembly.
responses.response: Your three-name proposal is the better-attributed version of B035, since it keeps the Vancouver group together and avoids the Anderson and Langer lipidoid dispute, and it answers part of my round-1 objection. What remains for me is the question you raised yourself, whether this is chemistry or pharmaceutical engineering after the 2023 Medicine prize, and the fact that MacLachlan's and Anderson's contributions are then left out. I still rank B035 as my second alternative, and I would rank it ahead of B068, because its maturity is not in doubt.

responses.point: Prefers B063 and weighs the fact that all eight members ranked it, while acknowledging that no PROTAC is approved and that the cut omits Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto.
responses.response: I take your point that breadth across all eight ballots is informative, and I do not dismiss it. I weigh it as evidence that nobody doubts the interest of the field, not as evidence that it is ready for a prize this year, since the same members mostly placed it fourth. On your question about clinical milestones, my own threshold would be a first regulatory approval or pivotal-trial success for a degrader, which may come within a few years and could change my ordering.

uncertainties: Whether colleagues regard zeolite and molecular-sieve design as distinct enough from the 2025 framework-materials prize.
Which three of Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu and Tsapatsis are the most decisive; my choice is partly subjective and I have not independently verified industrial attribution.
Whether a first degrader approval, which could come soon, would remove my main objection to B063 and change my ordering.
Whether the committee will accept a single mature design-principle prize over a plurality position whose three supporters agree on names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict with any named candidate is apparent from my profile, and I have no documented collaboration with Corma, Davis, Zones, Yu or Tsapatsis. My research is on electron crystallography of zeolites and other porous materials, so B051 is close to my field. This proximity was raised in round 1 and no colleague asked for recusal; I regard it as a bias to be weighed and will accept the committee's view if it prefers that I abstain on B051. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on any shortlisted candidate.
